catalog.name: Atmospheric Dynamics & Water Vapor
catalog.description: Atmospheric dynamics and water vapor products from NASA missions providing essential information about atmospheric moisture transport, weather patterns, and precipitation processes affecting water resources.

info.name: Attribution
info.content: Atmospheric products from NASA AIRS, GEOS, MERRA-2, and MODIS missions. Processing by NASA Goddard Earth Sciences Data and Information Services Center (GES DISC) and Global Modeling and Assimilation Office (GMAO). Contact: earthdata-support@nasa.gov

info.name: License
info.content: NASA data is generally available for public use. Atmospheric products support weather analysis, water resource forecasting, and climate research applications.

info.name: Hydrological Relevance
info.content: Atmospheric water vapor, wind patterns, and pressure systems control precipitation distribution, evaporation rates, and moisture transport, making these products essential for water resource assessment.

info.name: Weather-Water Connections
info.content: Understanding atmospheric dynamics enables improved precipitation forecasting, drought prediction, and assessment of atmospheric rivers and moisture transport affecting regional water resources.

members.name: Water Vapor & Humidity
members.description: Atmospheric water vapor and humidity products showing moisture content and transport in the atmosphere.

members.name: AIRS Air Temperature (Daily Day)
members.description: Daily daytime air temperature from AIRS infrared sounder providing high-accuracy temperature measurements for weather and climate applications.

info.name: Background
info.content: AIRS (Atmospheric Infrared Sounder) measures atmospheric water vapor using thermal infrared spectroscopy, providing high-accuracy humidity profiles and total column water vapor.

info.name: Measurement Principle
info.content: Uses thermal infrared absorption lines to retrieve atmospheric water vapor with high vertical resolution and radiometric accuracy

info.name: Measurement Units
info.content: Total column water vapor in millimeters (mm) or grams per square centimeter (g/cm²)

info.name: Spatial Resolution
info.content: 50 km spatial resolution with global coverage, suitable for regional to global scale moisture analysis

info.name: Temporal Coverage
info.content: September 2002 to present, providing 20+ years of high-quality atmospheric moisture data

info.name: All-Weather Capability
info.content: Infrared sounding provides some capability to measure water vapor through clouds, enhancing temporal coverage

info.name: Hydrological Applications
info.content: Water vapor measurements are essential for precipitation forecasting, atmospheric river detection, and understanding moisture transport affecting regional water resources

info.name: Applications
info.content: Weather forecasting, precipitation prediction, atmospheric river tracking, drought monitoring, water resource planning

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA AIRS mission team, NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL)

members.name: MODIS Cloud Water Path (Daily)
members.description: Daily cloud water path from MODIS Terra satellite providing high-resolution cloud liquid water content measurements for weather analysis.

info.name: Background
info.content: MODIS measures atmospheric water vapor using near-infrared absorption bands, providing high spatial resolution measurements of atmospheric moisture content.

info.name: High Resolution
info.content: 1 km spatial resolution enabling detailed analysis of moisture patterns and gradients

info.name: Clear Sky Retrievals
info.content: MODIS water vapor retrievals require clear sky conditions, providing high-quality measurements where clouds are absent

info.name: Complementary Coverage
info.content: Combined with AIRS data, provides comprehensive atmospheric moisture monitoring with different spatial resolutions and measurement capabilities

info.name: Applications
info.content: High-resolution moisture analysis, local weather patterns, convective initiation studies, detailed atmospheric moisture mapping

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA MODIS mission team, atmospheric products development teams

members.name: MERRA-2 Air Temperature (Monthly)
members.description: Monthly air temperature from MERRA-2 reanalysis providing comprehensive atmospheric temperature analysis with meteorological context.

info.name: Background
info.content: MERRA-2 (Modern-Era Retrospective analysis for Research and Applications) provides air temperature through advanced data assimilation combining observations with atmospheric models.

info.name: Data Assimilation
info.content: Combines satellite observations, radiosondes, and surface measurements to provide meteorologically consistent temperature fields

info.name: Measurement Units
info.content: Air temperature in degrees Celsius (°C) or Kelvin (K)

info.name: Vertical Levels
info.content: Surface air temperature at 2 meters above ground level, providing near-surface temperature conditions

info.name: Long-term Record
info.content: 1980 to present, providing 40+ years of consistent atmospheric moisture reanalysis

info.name: Meteorological Context
info.content: Part of comprehensive reanalysis system including winds, pressure, and temperature for complete atmospheric state

info.name: Applications
info.content: Climate studies, long-term temperature trend analysis, atmospheric model validation, weather pattern research

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA Global Modeling and Assimilation Office (GMAO), MERRA-2 reanalysis team

members.name: Atmospheric Pressure & Circulation
members.description: Atmospheric pressure and circulation patterns controlling weather systems and moisture transport.

members.name: MERRA-2 Surface Pressure (Monthly)
members.description: Monthly surface pressure from MERRA-2 reanalysis showing pressure systems and weather patterns affecting precipitation and water resources.

info.name: Background
info.content: Surface pressure patterns control weather systems, storm tracks, and precipitation distribution, making pressure analysis essential for water resource forecasting.

info.name: Measurement Units
info.content: Surface pressure in hectopascals (hPa) or millibars (mb)

info.name: Weather System Identification
info.content: Pressure patterns reveal high and low pressure systems, fronts, and storm tracks that control precipitation distribution

info.name: Seasonal Patterns
info.content: Pressure climatology shows monsoon systems, seasonal pressure migrations, and climate patterns affecting regional water resources

info.name: Forecast Applications
info.content: Pressure patterns are fundamental for weather forecasting and predicting precipitation events affecting water resources

info.name: Applications
info.content: Weather analysis, storm tracking, seasonal forecasting, climate pattern identification, water resource planning

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA Global Modeling and Assimilation Office (GMAO), MERRA-2 reanalysis team

members.name: MERRA-2 Wind Speed (Monthly)
members.description: Monthly wind speed from MERRA-2 showing atmospheric circulation patterns and moisture transport.

info.name: Background
info.content: Atmospheric winds transport moisture, control storm movement, and determine precipitation patterns, making wind analysis crucial for water resource assessment.

info.name: Measurement Units
info.content: Wind speed in meters per second (m/s) with directional components

info.name: Moisture Transport
info.content: Wind patterns control atmospheric moisture transport, including atmospheric rivers and monsoon circulations affecting regional water resources

info.name: Storm Tracking
info.content: Wind patterns enable tracking of storm systems, tropical cyclones, and weather fronts that produce precipitation

info.name: Circulation Analysis
info.content: Wind patterns reveal large-scale circulation features like jet streams, trade winds, and monsoon systems

info.name: Applications
info.content: Storm tracking, moisture transport analysis, seasonal circulation studies, atmospheric river detection, weather pattern analysis

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA Global Modeling and Assimilation Office (GMAO), MERRA-2 reanalysis team

members.name: Cloud Properties & Atmospheric Stability
members.description: Cloud properties and atmospheric stability indicators affecting precipitation formation and weather development.

members.name: MODIS Cloud Water Path (Terra)
members.description: Cloud water path from MODIS Terra indicating cloud liquid water content and potential for precipitation development.

info.name: Background
info.content: Cloud fraction represents the percentage of area covered by clouds, providing information about cloudiness patterns and potential for precipitation.

info.name: Measurement Units
info.content: Cloud fraction as percentage (0-100%) of grid cell covered by clouds

info.name: Precipitation Potential
info.content: High cloud fractions often indicate conditions conducive to precipitation formation and weather system development

info.name: Spatial Resolution
info.content: 1 km spatial resolution enabling detailed cloud pattern analysis

info.name: Diurnal Patterns
info.content: Cloud fraction patterns reveal diurnal cycles of convective activity and weather system development

info.name: Applications
info.content: Weather pattern analysis, convective activity monitoring, precipitation forecasting support, climate studies

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA MODIS mission team, cloud property algorithm teams

members.name: AIRS Air Temperature (Daily Night)
members.description: Daily nighttime air temperature from AIRS infrared sounder providing high-accuracy temperature measurements for weather and climate applications.

info.name: Background
info.content: Atmospheric stability indices indicate the tendency of the atmosphere to support or suppress vertical motion and convective activity that leads to precipitation.

info.name: Stability Measures
info.content: Includes various stability parameters such as convective available potential energy (CAPE) and convective inhibition (CIN)

info.name: Convective Potential
info.content: Stability indices help identify conditions favorable for thunderstorm development and intense precipitation events

info.name: Forecast Applications
info.content: Stability parameters are essential for predicting convective weather and associated precipitation patterns

info.name: Water Resource Relevance
info.content: Convective precipitation often produces intense rainfall events important for flash flood forecasting and water resource management

info.name: Applications
info.content: Severe weather forecasting, convective precipitation prediction, flash flood assessment, atmospheric instability analysis

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA AIRS mission team, atmospheric stability algorithm teams

members.name: Advanced Atmospheric Circulation
members.description: Advanced atmospheric circulation datasets from MERRA-2 reanalysis providing comprehensive surface wind and pressure patterns for detailed weather and climate analysis.

members.name: Surface Wind Speed (Monthly)
members.description: Monthly surface wind speed from MERRA-2 reanalysis providing comprehensive global wind patterns for atmospheric circulation analysis and wind energy applications.

info.name: Background
info.content: Surface wind speed from MERRA-2 provides model-based estimates of near-surface wind patterns by integrating observations with atmospheric modeling, offering consistent global wind climatology for multiple applications.

info.name: Meteorological Significance
info.content: Surface winds drive atmospheric moisture transport, control evaporation rates, influence storm development, and determine air mass movement patterns critical for weather and climate

info.name: Hydrological Applications
info.content: Wind patterns control evaporation from water bodies, soil moisture loss, atmospheric moisture transport, and regional precipitation patterns affecting water resource availability

info.name: Seasonal Patterns
info.content: Monthly resolution reveals seasonal wind patterns including monsoon circulations, trade wind variations, and storm track changes affecting regional water resources

info.name: Spatial Resolution
info.content: 0.5° × 0.625° global grid providing detailed regional wind patterns suitable for climate analysis and atmospheric circulation studies

info.name: Temporal Coverage
info.content: 1980 to present, providing over 40 years of consistent wind data for long-term climate analysis and trend detection

info.name: Climate Applications
info.content: Climate model validation, long-term circulation trend analysis, monsoon system evaluation, atmospheric transport studies, climate change impact assessment

info.name: Energy Applications
info.content: Wind energy resource assessment, wind power potential mapping, renewable energy planning, wind farm site evaluation

info.name: Environmental Applications
info.content: Air quality modeling, pollutant transport analysis, dust storm tracking, wildfire smoke dispersion, atmospheric chemistry studies

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA MERRA-2 reanalysis, NASA Global Modeling and Assimilation Office (GMAO), surface wind analysis team

members.name: Surface Pressure (Monthly)
members.description: Monthly surface pressure from MERRA-2 reanalysis showing atmospheric pressure patterns that control weather systems, storm development, and large-scale atmospheric circulation.

info.name: Background
info.content: Surface atmospheric pressure is a fundamental meteorological variable that controls weather patterns, storm systems, and large-scale atmospheric circulation affecting precipitation and water resources globally.

info.name: Weather System Control
info.content: Surface pressure patterns determine the formation and movement of high and low pressure systems, frontal boundaries, and storm tracks that produce precipitation

info.name: Circulation Patterns
info.content: Pressure gradients drive wind patterns and atmospheric circulation including monsoons, trade winds, and seasonal pressure oscillations affecting regional water resources

info.name: Storm Development
info.content: Low pressure systems are associated with storm development, cyclone formation, and precipitation events, while high pressure systems typically bring clear, dry conditions

info.name: Seasonal Oscillations
info.content: Monthly resolution captures seasonal pressure variations including monsoon systems, polar oscillations, and other climate patterns affecting regional precipitation

info.name: Climate Indices
info.content: Surface pressure data is used to calculate climate indices like the Southern Oscillation Index, Arctic Oscillation, and other teleconnection patterns

info.name: Weather Prediction
info.content: Surface pressure patterns are fundamental for weather forecasting, storm tracking, and understanding atmospheric dynamics affecting water resources

info.name: Long-term Analysis
info.content: 40+ year MERRA-2 record enables analysis of long-term pressure trends, climate variability, and changing atmospheric circulation patterns

info.name: Research Applications
info.content: Atmospheric dynamics research, climate variability studies, teleconnection analysis, atmospheric circulation modeling, weather pattern classification

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA MERRA-2 reanalysis, NASA Global Modeling and Assimilation Office (GMAO), atmospheric pressure analysis team

members.name: Earth's Energy Balance
members.description: Earth's energy balance datasets measuring incoming solar radiation and outgoing longwave radiation, fundamental for understanding climate processes and surface energy budgets.

members.name: Outgoing Longwave Radiation (Daily)
members.description: Daily clear-sky outgoing longwave radiation from AIRS satellite measurements showing Earth's thermal emission to space, critical for understanding Earth's energy balance and climate processes.

info.name: Background
info.content: Outgoing Longwave Radiation (OLR) represents the thermal energy emitted by Earth to space, serving as a critical component of Earth's energy balance and a key indicator of atmospheric and surface conditions.

info.name: Energy Balance Significance
info.content: OLR represents the 'cooling' side of Earth's energy balance, balancing incoming solar radiation. Changes in OLR affect global temperature and climate stability

info.name: Clear Sky Conditions
info.content: Clear-sky OLR measurements exclude cloud effects, providing direct information about surface and atmospheric thermal emissions without cloud interference

info.name: Temperature Relationship
info.content: OLR is directly related to surface and atmospheric temperatures - higher temperatures produce more longwave emission, lower temperatures produce less

info.name: Regional Variations
info.content: OLR varies geographically with surface type, elevation, and atmospheric conditions, providing insights into regional energy balance and climate characteristics

info.name: Climate Applications
info.content: Essential for climate model validation, greenhouse effect studies, climate sensitivity analysis, and understanding radiative forcing and climate feedbacks

info.name: Seasonal Patterns
info.content: Daily measurements reveal seasonal and diurnal cycles of thermal emission, providing insights into surface heating patterns and atmospheric dynamics

info.name: Weather Applications
info.content: OLR patterns can indicate atmospheric stability, convective activity, and temperature distributions affecting weather development and water vapor processes

info.name: Research Applications
info.content: Climate change studies, radiative transfer research, atmospheric physics, surface energy balance validation, climate model evaluation

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA AIRS mission team, NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), atmospheric radiation measurement team

members.name: Incident Solar Radiation Over Land (Monthly)
members.description: Monthly incident solar radiation over land surfaces from MERRA-2 reanalysis showing the solar energy reaching Earth's land surface, fundamental for understanding surface energy budgets and climate processes.

info.name: Background
info.content: Incident shortwave radiation represents the solar energy reaching Earth's land surface after atmospheric attenuation, providing the primary energy source for surface heating, photosynthesis, and the hydrological cycle.

info.name: Energy Source
info.content: Solar radiation is the fundamental energy source driving Earth's climate system, surface heating, evaporation, photosynthesis, and nearly all atmospheric and hydrological processes

info.name: Land Surface Focus
info.content: This product specifically measures solar radiation reaching land surfaces, excluding ocean areas to focus on terrestrial energy balance and land-atmosphere interactions

info.name: Atmospheric Effects
info.content: Accounts for atmospheric absorption and scattering by gases, aerosols, and clouds, providing the actual solar energy available at the surface rather than theoretical top-of-atmosphere values

info.name: Seasonal Variations
info.content: Monthly resolution captures seasonal cycles of solar radiation driven by Earth's orbital geometry, providing insights into seasonal energy availability and climate patterns

info.name: Surface Energy Balance
info.content: Critical component of surface energy balance calculations, determining surface heating, temperature patterns, and energy available for evaporation and plant processes

info.name: Hydrological Relevance
info.content: Solar radiation drives evaporation from surface water and soil, plant transpiration, and atmospheric moisture processes that control the water cycle

info.name: Agricultural Applications
info.content: Essential for crop modeling, photosynthesis calculations, growing season analysis, and agricultural productivity assessment based on available solar energy

info.name: Climate Applications
info.content: Fundamental for climate modeling, surface temperature prediction, energy balance validation, and understanding land-atmosphere coupling processes

info.name: Renewable Energy Applications
info.content: Critical for solar energy resource assessment, photovoltaic potential mapping, renewable energy planning, and solar power system design

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA MERRA-2 reanalysis, NASA Global Modeling and Assimilation Office (GMAO), surface radiation analysis team
